text:
Kiana M: Quick question — UX tie between per-route saved views and model fallback behavior. Currently if route /api/chat is pinned to model:v2 we show per-route saved queries tied to that route. But if runtime routing falls back to model:v1 (quota/burst) the console still shows v2 metrics and savedviews. Confusing for users.

Samir: Yeah that's been reported. Do we want the console to always reflect the configured pin (route-level intent) or the actual runtime routing (what served the request)? :thinking:

Leo: my vote -> surface the configured pin by default (intent) and surface a clear badge for last-served-model + link to telemetry. Intent is what users set; metrics can be noisy if we flip view to runtime by default.

Andrea: agree on intent-first, but we should have a prominent affordance: small pill "served: v1 (fallback)" with a hover pop that shows time-series of serve-rate by model for that route. Users can then toggle the view to "Actual served" which will swap savedquery suggestions to model:v1 variants.

Kiana M: That toggle is interesting. UX question: when user toggles to "Actual served", which savedviews do we show? Only saved queries explicitly scoped to model:v1? Or fall back to route-scope ones? Mixed results could be confusing.

Maria: propose precedence: 1) model-scoped savedviews (if user explicitly selected model view) 2) route-scoped savedviews (route intent) 3) global savedviews. If user toggles to Actual-served, show model-scoped first. Also add small tooltip: "Showing views most relevant to what actually answered requests".

Samir: Implementation note — our API for savedviews currently keys by route_id and team_id. We don't have a first-class model scope in the savedviews index. We'll need a small migration: add optional model_tag to savedview metadata and an index for (route_id, model_tag).

Jun (DevEx): tagging savedviews with model_tag is doable. Need to update Console create modal and SDK. Backwards compatible: newly created views can include model_tag; existing views default to no model_tag.

Leo: telemetry-wise, we need to show sampling breakdown. When user toggles "Actual served" we should also switch the telemetry sampling window to the serve-attribution stream (the one that tracks fallback events) so the cost-preview numbers match.

Kiana M: good call. What about rollouts + canary: If model:v2 is canary for 10% traffic and fallback increases v1 to 90%, the console should warn if savedviews were validated against v2 only. Maybe a small banner: "Saved views were evaluated on model:v2 (10% traffic). Actual traffic served mostly by v1 — metrics may differ." :warning:

Andrea: UX mock idea — right under the route header show a compact "Evaluation coverage" bar with segments for models (click to expand). Clicking a segment opens (a) telemetry histogram and (b) a checkbox: "Limit savedviews suggestions to this model's variants".

Samir: security/quotas angle — when Dedicated customers have strict quotas, we already silently enforce fallbacks to cheaper quantized variants. We need to ensure console's cost-preview and quota-alert rules execute against the effective model in the last N minutes, not only the configured pin.

deploy-bot: [deploy] services/console v2.8.1 started rolling batch of telemetry UI changes (canary 5%): https://ci.example/redwood/console/1234 :rocket:

Maria: action items: 1) create savedview metadata migration RFC (Samir + Jun) 2) small UX wire for toggle + badge (Andrea + Kiana) 3) telemetry API change to expose serve-by-model windows and serve attribution (Leo + Eng-ML) 4) ensure cost-preview reads from "effective model window" (Samir)

Kiana M: cool — I'll own the UX ticket and draft copy for the banners/tooltips. Can someone add a quick prototype of the compact coverage bar in Figma? Andrea?

Andrea: on it. Will drop a short prototype and tag this thread when ready. :paintbrush:

Samir: I'll start the RFC scaffold and put a note about index performance for (route_id, model_tag). Probably need a redis secondary index for quick lookups.

Jun (DevEx): I'll add a CLI flag for migrating existing savedviews to allow optional model_tag assignment so we don't block rollout.

Kiana M: Thanks all — let's reconvene after prototypes. If anyone runs into edgecases (multi-route savedviews, shared models across routes) drop them here.

Leo: one more edgecase: per-tenant model aliasing (customers map model:v2 -> internal model:redwood-large-qa). Need the model_tag to be the canonical alias we use in routing decisions, not the user alias. We'll note that in RFC.

Maria: noted. ending thread with a thumbs up.

Kiana M: :thumbsup:
